root_cause.text: mac80211’s `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l()` in `net/mac80211/mlme.c` always read a link-map presence byte from TTLM elements, even when `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` indicated the default mapping and no presence field exists, causing an off-by-one parse/read past the element end.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` to execute only when `!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP)`, and the CVE description explicitly says default-mapping TTLMs “do not contain any link mapping presence indicator” and that mac80211 “would also read one byte beyond the end of the element.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip parsing the link map presence byte when the default link map control bit is set to avoid misreading the TTLM payload.
intent_record.what: The code that reads `link_map_presence` was moved behind a conditional: instead of always assigning `link_map_presence = *pos;` and incrementing `pos`, it now does so only when `!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP)` is true. The surrounding `switch_time` parsing code is unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser no longer consumes a link map presence byte when the control field indicates the default link map is used. This preserves the correct buffer position for subsequent optional fields, preventing misparsing of the TLV layout when `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` is set.

The change directly matches the root cause: it stops reading the link-map presence byte when the default-link-map control bit means that field is absent, preventing the off-by-one read past the TTLM element end.

candidates.rationale: This statement unconditionally reads a link-map presence byte from the TTLM element. The vulnerability occurs when the default-link-map control bit is set and no presence field exists, so this read goes past the valid element payload.
After the unconditional presence-byte read, this advances the parse cursor even when the byte should not be present, contributing to the off-by-one parse past the end of the TTLM element.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line unconditionally reads a link-map presence byte from the TTLM element. When IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP indicates the default mapping, that byte is absent, so this read goes past the valid element payload and triggers the off-by-one parse/read.
This line advances the parser as if a presence byte were always present. In the default-link-map case, it contributes to parsing beyond the end of the TTLM element.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body for `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l()` already contains the relevant handling that avoids the reported bug. It reads the presence byte unconditionally at `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;`, but crucially it then checks `if (control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP) { ttlm_info->map = 0xffff; return 0; }` before any use of the presence byte for non-default maps. The vulnerable root cause was that the parser always consumed a link-map presence byte even when `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` indicated the default mapping and no presence field exists, causing an off-by-one read. In this snippet, that exact condition is guarded by the `DEF_LINK_MAP` early return, so the vulnerable construct is not present in a harmful form here. The rest of the parsing (`if (link_map_presence != 0xff) ...`, `ttlm_info->map = ieee80211_get_ttlm(...)`) only applies when the default-map flag is not set. Therefore, this version already contains the fix rather than the bug.
